title: Shooting at U.S. Seattle food festival leaves 2 dead, wounds 5
summary: Two people were killed, and five others were wounded in a shooting on Sunday (July 26, 2026) evening during a food festival at an events complex near the Space Needle in Seattle, a city fire department spokesperson said.

title: Three-wheeler driver killed in Gothatuwa road accident - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - A three-wheeler driver was killed in a road accident in the Gothatuwa area this morning (27), Police said.

The accident occurred when a three-wheeler travelling from Kolonnawa towards Gothatuwa collided with a private bus.

The three-wheeler driver died at the scene, while another person who sustained injuries was admitted to the Colombo National Hospital for treatment.

Kolonnawa Police are conducting further investigations into the incident.

title: AI will take away SL’s business outsourcing revenue: MP - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Indicating that artificial intelligence (AI) will affect Sri Lanka's economy in an unimaginable way, Opposition MP Ravi Karunanayake said it has already begun to take away the revenue which the country has been generating out of business process outsourcing.

"The emergence of AI has already made one company engage in providing business process outsourcing service to reduce salaries for its employees," he added.

Also, the MP said the reduction in Sri Lanka's birth rate will have a negative effect on the country.

"The fact of the matter is that Sri Lanka's aging population will increase as a result of the reduced birth rate, which is even less than one percent. Sri Lanka will have to face certain social and economic issues with the increase of the aging population," he said.

Furthermore, he said Sri Lanka should focus on energy security in the wake of hostilities in the Middle East.

"Sri Lanka should focus on making the rupee stable so that the increase of oil prices will be manageable with a stable local currency."

"Another fact which the country should focus is power. There could be a high demand for renewable energy later this year and early next year with the El Nino phenomenon which is expected to hit Sri Lanka. Sri Lanka should focus on renewable energy in that scenario," the MP also said.

title: Colombo sees over 250 fire incidents so far this year - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - A total of 258 fire incidents have been reported in Colombo and its surrounding areas during this year, the Fire Service Department has revealed.

According to the Department, 17 rescue operations were carried out in connection with these fire incidents during the same period.

Officials noted that 382 fire incidents were recorded in the Colombo District throughout last year, along with 46 rescue operations.

The Department stressed that the fact that 258 fire incidents have already been reported in the Colombo District from January to date this year is a matter that warrants serious attention.

In addition to fire-related incidents, the Fire Service Department has also responded to 13 emergency calls so far this year.

These included rescue operations related to road obstructions, fallen trees, and road traffic accidents.

The Department said investigations have identified several key factors contributing to the rise in fire incidents, including the lack of adequate fire safety measures at workplaces, failure to respond promptly to emergencies, unsafe electrical installations and practices in homes and commercial premises, and the prevailing dry weather conditions.

title: Seek prompt medical treatment if children’s fever persists over 24 hours: Health authorities - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - In the wake of growing risk of dengue spread, Health authorities urged parents to seek prompt medical treatment without delay, if children's fever persists for more than 24 hours.

Director at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital for Children in Colombo, Dr. Pradeep Ratnasekara advised parents not to resort to unscientific home remedies claiming that staying at home and using home remedies wastes the time available to treat the child.

He urged parents to take the child to the nearest government hospital and seek proper medical advice.

Dr. Ratnasekara said around 50 children infected with dengue are currently receiving treatment at the Lady Ridgeway Hospital and that about one-fourth of them are in critical condition.

He said if this situation worsens further, issues regarding hospital capacity could arise.

"I must particularly state that it is not necessary to bring your child to the Lady Ridgeway Hospital all the way from distant areas. The main reason for many deaths is late arrival at the hospital. If a fever persists for more than 24 hours, it is appropriate to seek medical advice. Instead of staying at home for days doing home remedies and wasting your valuable time along with the time required to provide the necessary treatment for the child, it is extremely important to bring them to a qualified doctor or a government doctor very quickly," he said.

He said only one dengue death has been reported in the Lady Ridgeway Hospital.

title: Oil market alarming for Sri Lanka, CPC seeks meeting with President - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - With the global oil market remaining volatile due to tensions in the Middle East, the Ceylon Petroleum Corporation (CPC) has sought an urgent meeting with President Anura Kumara Dissanayake to discuss fresh measures to mitigate the impact, an official said.

Asserting that the global oil market situation is alarming for Sri Lanka, CPC Chairman D.J. Rajakaruna told the Daily Mirror that the public should be aware of the worsening trend.

He said diesel prices had surged by 45 per cent and petrol prices by 30 per cent compared with the rates that prevailed at the beginning of this month. Crude oil prices have also increased sharply since then, making the situation increasingly difficult for Sri Lanka, a country that is entirely dependent on fuel imports.

"We have sought a meeting with the President to discuss what needs to be done. Consumption reduction is needed," he said.

He said other retail fuel distributors in the domestic market had also cited difficulties in selling fuel at the current prices.

The price of physical crude oil cargoes in the Middle East, Europe and Africa jumped this week to two-month highs, with some nearing US$110 a barrel, as supply disruptions linked to the conflicts involving Iran and Ukraine left buyers scrambling to secure prompt supplies from other sources, Reuters reported.

Mr. Rajakaruna said the dry spell triggered by El Niño weather conditions had reduced hydropower generation capacity, placing further strain on the demand for fuel used in power generation.

"This is yet another serious challenge for us. We are now compelled to release increasing quantities of fuel from our stocks to generate power in the absence of adequate hydropower generation," he said.

title: Sajith denies political deal with BASL President - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Opposition Leader Sajith Premadasa yesterday denied the allegation made by National People's Power (NPP) MP Asitha Niroshana that Bar Association of Sri Lanka (BASL) President Rajiv Amarasuriya had got into a political deal with him.

"The government cannot defend its plan to change the retirement age of judges. A JVP MP stood in Parliament and accused me of bribing the Bar Association to oppose it.What a shameless accusation. I challenge MP Asitha Niroshana to come outside Parliament and repeat this," Mr. Premadasa said in his latest X message.

Meanwhile, MP Niroshana and other NPP members came under fire by Free Lawyers Association Convenor Maithri Gunaratne who posed a challenge to them. "We challenge NPP members to come out in the open and make this allegation against Amarasuriya. Millions can be claimed as damages from NPP MPs if they make the allegation outside Parliament," he said.

Gunaratne told media that the BASL President opposed the move to extend the retirement age of Judges from the very inception.

title: Police OIC becomes hit and run driver - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Buddhika Kumarasiri

Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - A hit and run driver, allegedly a senior police official, who knocked down two young women at two locations and fled in his car was arrested by Meegoda Police yesterday.

Police said the suspect was a Chief Inspector (CI) and OIC of a Special Investigation Unit in the Homagama SSP Division.

He had caused the two accidents at 11.30 pm and 11.57 pm on Saturday (25), one at Wataraka and the other near the Meegoda filling station.

Investigations revealed that he was under the influence of liquor at the time of the incident. He was to be produced before the Homagama magistrate yesterday.

title: Sri Lanka’s underworld violence escalates - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Sri Lanka has recorded 22 shooting incidents so far this year, leaving 15 people dead and 12 others injured. Nearly half of these incidents, 10 in total, were reported within the two-week period between July 11 and July 25.

The 10 shootings during this period claimed three lives and left five people injured. The incidents have ranged from targeted killings and attacks linked to organized criminal groups. Several other incidents resulted in property damage or targeted individuals without causing casualties. Police have made a number of arrests in connection with the shootings, while investigations into the remaining cases are continuing.

Meanwhile, Sri Lanka Police have attributed the recent spate of shootings across the country to rival drug trafficking networks, saying the attacks are primarily driven by organized criminal disputes, contract killings, and attempts to intimidate rival groups.

Responding to questions about the ten shootings reported over the past two weeks, including the latest incident on Saturday, Police Spokesman Assistant Superintendent of Police (ASP) F.U. Wootler said every incident investigated so far has shown links to organized crime and the illegal drug trade.

According to the Police Spokesman, the shootings are largely the result of rival criminal groups attempting to eliminate competitors, settle financial disputes, and prevent opposing gangs from expanding their influence.

He said that many of the individuals believed to be orchestrating the attacks are currently operating from overseas, while the intended victims are often relatives or associates of rival gang members. Such attacks, he said, are carried out to intimidate opponents and send a message to competing criminal networks.

ASP Wootler said the Sri Lanka Police, under the direct guidance of the Inspector General of Police, have intensified intelligence operations, including telephone and communications analysis, to identify those responsible for planning and carrying out the attacks.

Referring to the fatal shooting in Bellanwila on July 25, he said that police arrested two suspects within an hour of the incident. According to investigators, one of those arrested is believed to be the gunman while the other allegedly rode the motorcycle used in the attack. Police also found evidence indicating that both suspects were heavily addicted to narcotics.

The Police Spokesman further revealed that investigators are increasingly finding that drugs, rather than cash, are being used as payment for contract killings. He said some suspects are allegedly willing to carry out murders in exchange for small quantities of narcotics.

Explaining why shootings appear to occur in clusters after relatively quiet periods, ASP Wootler said criminal groups wait until they have located their intended targets and identified opportunities when police presence is limited before carrying out attacks.

He acknowledged that it is impossible to deploy police officers at every location but said law enforcement agencies continue to rely on intelligence-led operations to prevent violent crime. He said that police will continue to take strict action against organized criminal groups and those involved in drug-related violence.

Shootings reported across the country between July 11 - July 25

Gunmen riding a motorcycle opened fire at a house in the Neboda, Matugama on July 11, although no injuries were reported.

A suspected drug trafficker snatched a traffic police officer's service firearm and shot at him during a narcotics raid in Katunayake on July 15. The officer was injured.

A 26-year-old man from Kaduwela was shot and killed by unidentified gunmen on July 16 in Wandurabumulla, Navagamuwa.

A 56-year-old security guard was shot and injured on July 19 inside the "Nisala Sewana" Dehiwala–Mount Lavinia public cemetery.

A 24-year-old suspect was shot and injured by police in Bokundara, Piliyandala on July 19 when he attempted to assault the officers with a sword.

Unidentified gunmen travelling in a car opened several rounds of fire on a fisherman's home in Devinuwara on July 21. No injuries were reported.

The house of a police sergeant came under gunfire in the Walawala area of Beliatta on the night of Wednesday, July 22. The officer and family members escaped without injury.

A 39-year-old man was shot dead during a child's birthday party at a function hall in the Palliyawatta area of Wattala on the night of Thursday, on July 23

A shooting incident near the Kuppiyawatta cemetery in Dematagoda left one man seriously injured on July 23.

A 55-year-old restaurant owner was fatally shot near the entrance to the Bellanwila walking track along the Dehiwala–Boralesgamuwa Road on July 25.

title: Iran says it will halt strikes as long as US bombing pause holds
summary: Iran will halt its own attacks as long as the United States does the same, a senior Iranian official told Reuters on Sunday. The development comes as the United States pressed pause on its bombing campaign after President Donald Trump’s advisers told him they were running out of targets and expressed worries about depleting the U.S. arsenal.

title: Oil prices plunge 5% after U.S. and Iran halt attacks
summary: Oil prices plunged by more than 5% in early Asian trade on Monday as the U.S. and Iran halted attacks after two weeks of escalation that had driven Brent above $100.

title: Fresh controversy over Colombo national school's dry ration drive - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 27 (Daily Mirror) - Fresh controversy has erupted over the disputed dry ration collection drive at Thurstan College after the school's parents' union alleged that some of the donated food items had already expired and claimed the distribution programme had been shifted from Delft Island (Neduntheevu) to schools in Jaffna following media scrutiny.

The latest allegations come weeks after the parents' union claimed that Thurstan College had requested parents of students from Grades 1 to 13 to donate dry rations and school supplies for around 600 students in 10 schools on Delft Island, raising concerns over compulsory collections and the financial burden placed on families.

According to the parents' union, the principal had informed parents that the initiative was being conducted as part of a Health Promotion Programme under the Education Ministry. However, the union said Education Ministry officials later confirmed they were unaware of any such programme and that no approval had been granted.

The union also alleged that parents had been instructed not to publicise the collection drive.

In the latest development, the parents' union claimed that some of the dry rations collected from parents had already expired despite plans to distribute them on Tuesday (29). It further alleged that, following media scrutiny of the controversy, the principal abandoned the original plan to distribute the goods to schools on Delft Island and instead decided to send them to several schools in Jaffna.

According to the union, the goods are now expected to be handed over to the Jaffna Zonal Education Office.

The union also claimed that teachers had been instructed to report for duty and travel to Jaffna to participate in the distribution programme despite the project allegedly lacking Education Ministry approval.

Questioning the authority under which the programme was organised, the parents' union asked how the principal had been able to conduct a large-scale collection drive and distribution exercise without the ministry's permission.

The parents' union has also requested the Consumer Affairs Authority (CAA) to inspect the quality of the donated goods before they are distributed.

Some parents had previously claimed that individual classes collected goods worth more than Rs. 24,000, while also complaining about the financial burden imposed on families. The union had further alleged that students were earlier asked to contribute Rs. 500 each for Vesak lantern decorations.

A senior Education Ministry official previously told the Daily Mirror that the ministry was unaware of the programme and reiterated that no approval had been granted for such an initiative.

The Daily Mirror previously made several attempts to obtain a response from the Thurstan College principal, but those efforts were unsuccessful. Government policy maintains that while voluntary donations cannot be prohibited, schools have no legal authority to compel parents to make contributions.

title: Sri Lankan faces backlash over ‘ego-driven’ expansion plans, soaring maintenance costs and CEO vacuum - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
By Nishel Fernando

SriLankan Airlines’ new Chairman Dimal Arandara is drawing heavy scrutiny over an unconventional strategic proposal to balance the national carrier’s bloated staff-to-aircraft ratio by purchasing more aircraft instead of right-sizing the workforce.

Testifying before a recent parliamentary committee hearing, Arandara defended the push for fleet expansion as a statistical remedy for staffing imbalances.

“When you divide the number of staff by the 23 aircraft we have, the number of maintenance staff per aircraft is high. To address this, the fleet must definitely be increased,” Arandara told the committee.

The Chairman further attempted to justify the strategy by boasting about acquiring older aircraft at steeply discounted monthly lease rates. Pointing to large-scale savings on initial rentals, Arandara noted, “If we paid US$ 800,000 a month previously, from December we are paying US$ 43,000 for a wide body. resulting in a saving of US$ 370,000 per flight per month.”

He openly acknowledged the reliance on aging planes, stating, “Even when we lease, we are not leasing new aircraft; generally, we lease aircraft that are seven to eight years old,” which adds to a fleet with an average age of 12 years.

However, aviation analysts and critics argue this approach is fundamentally flawed and ignores the crippling reality of backend operational expenses. The strategy fails to take into account that the older the aircraft, the higher the maintenance costs. During the last financial year (FY26), while the airline’s total lease cost stood at US$ 78.6 million, maintenance costs skyrocketed to a staggering US$ 207.3 million for the year. Adding older planes to the fleet will only exacerbate this disproportionate maintenance burden, rapidly wiping out any operational savings made on the initial lease agreements.

Deploying additional aircraft without a corresponding surge in actual market demand also directly threatens the airline’s profitability. Industry experts caution that artificially adding capacity to a route negatively impacts yield and load factors, resulting in the dilution of route profits or, worse, a severe increase in existing route losses. This is a critical concern given the carrier’s bleak commercial performance.

According to a recently published business plan, 38 out of SriLankan Airlines’ 52 routes are already loss-making, a figure that notably includes all 15 of its routes to India.

The strategic direction championed by the current leadership has raised serious concerns regarding competency. Even the  recently appointed expert restructuring committee, headed by Senior Presidential Advisor on Digital Economy Dr. Hans Wijayasuriya, has been  criticised for lacking credible, dedicated aviation experts.

When questioned about strategic oversight, Arandara stated, “All these plans are studied by the expert committee appointed for restructuring... chaired by Dr. Hans,” yet observers note that neither the committee nor the Chairman himself possesses prior aviation expertise.

Further compounding the carrier’s commercial instability is the revelation that the airline has operated without a permanent Chief Executive Officer for over a year and four months. Despite receiving a vast number of applications—172 in the initial round and over 200 in the second—leadership indicated an inability to match the salary expectations of qualified foreign aviation executives, leaving the critical role vacant.

This leadership vacuum and the handling of the recruitment process drew sharp criticism from Chairman of the Sectoral Oversight Committee on Infrastructure and Strategic Development MP S. M. Marikkar, who questioned the ongoing delays and the board’s apparent disregard for local talent.

“It is a tragic situation that for about a year and four months we haven’t been able to find a CEO. We cannot find someone from within, nor can we find someone externally. It shows exactly where we stand as an airline,” Marikkar pointed out during the committee session.

Calling out the heavy reliance on international headhunting, he challenged the committee, asking, “Are there really no capable people in Sri Lanka for this?”

Addressing the recruitment panel’s stringent demands for comprehensive aviation experience, Marikkar argued that a successful business leader does not need to be a technical master of every single operational division. “A CEO doesn’t need to have expertise in every single area,” he stated. “That is why there are specialists and department heads. Ultimately, it is about how it is managed.”

Highlighting the untapped potential of domestic corporate leadership, he noted, “We have seen plenty of private sector companies where people who came up from within the organization run the companies better than these experts.”

title: Legal experts flag unique compliance landscape in staggered PDPA rollout - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Dushyantha Perera

The enforcement of Sri Lanka’s Personal Data Protection Act (PDPA) No. 9 of 2022 has taken a definitive step forward with a recent gazette notification declaring January 1, 2027, as the operational date for several key sections.

Issued by President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in his capacity as Minister of Digital Economy on July 22, 2026, under Gazette Extraordinary No. 2498/16, the directive brings a staggered approach to data privacy enforcement.

This establishes core obligations for data controllers and processors while deferring certain data subject rights and penal provisions.

Legal experts note that this phased rollout creates an unusual yet practical enforcement environment. Dushyantha Perera, Partner and Head of Corporate and Commercial Law at Sudath Perera Associates, describes the gazette as a “significant development in the data privacy framework in Sri Lanka”. He highlights that “controllers and processors will soon be subject to legally enforceable obligations relating to the collection, processing, disclosure and governance of personal data”. Concurrently, the Data Protection Authority (DPA), which has been operational under Part V since July 2023, will be fully enabled to exercise its supervisory and enforcement functions.

The impending 2027 deadline does not activate all aspects of the PDPA. Perera points out that Part II of the Act, which governs the rights of data subjects, is yet to be brought into force. This means “statutory rights of data subjects such as access, rectification, erasure, objection and appeal to the DPA are not yet enforceable”. Likewise, Part IV, regulating the dissemination of solicited messages, and Part VII, concerning administrative penalties, have also been deferred.

According to Perera, “this development ‘appears’ to create an interesting and somewhat unusual compliance/enforcement landscape”. He notes that while the DPA can potentially inquire into and issue directives regarding failures by controllers and processors to comply with obligations under Part I or III, its punitive powers are restricted. This oversight can potentially extend to awarding compensation to persons who have suffered harm, loss, or damage due to contraventions of the relevant provisions by controllers and processors. However, because Part II is not in force, it does not extend to the statutory rights of data subjects under that part of the Act.

Furthermore, without Part VII in operation, “the DPA will not have the power to impose administrative penalties on non-compliant organizations” starting from January 1, 2027. Despite this limitation, legal professionals and digital policy analysts commend the staggered approach. Perera states, “This incremental/staggered approach to implementation of the Act does, however, make sense and is commendable”. He warns that organizations now have a legally binding obligation to start establishing their privacy compliance frameworks, as they will potentially be in violation of Sri Lanka’s generally applicable data protection law come the new year if they do not comply. Deferring the imposition of data subject rights allows organizations to first establish these vital initial structures.

Industry analysts echo this sentiment, emphasizing that this window sends a clear signal to build sustainable privacy governance rather than treating the new year merely as a hard compliance deadline. The DPA will still wield considerable influence, including conducting compliance evaluations, issuing course corrections, and executing compensation directives under section 35 of the Act, albeit without immediate administrative penal authority. (NF)

title: Former Envoy Kananathan salutes Liberia on 179th Independence Day, signals renewable energy partnership initiative - Breaking News | Daily Mirror
summary:
Colombo, July 26 (Daily Mirror) - Former Envoy Ambassador Kananathan has extended his warmest congratulations today to His Excellency President Joseph Nyuma Boakai,  the Government, and the people of the Republic of Liberia on the occasion of the country’s 179th Independence Day.

In his message, Kananathan commended Liberia’s enduring legacy as Africa’s oldest republic and expressed his admiration for the resilience, unity, and determination of the Liberian people in advancing peace, democracy, and national development.

“As Liberia celebrates this important national milestone, I extend my sincere best wishes to President Boakai and all Liberians. Kananathan said .

Kananathan also reaffirmed his commitment to strengthening ties with Liberia through sustainable development initiatives. He noted that he is currently in the process of initiating a renewable energy project in Liberia, aimed at supporting the country’s clean energy transition, promoting economic growth, and expanding access to sustainable power solutions.

He expressed confidence that the planned initiative would contribute to Liberia’s long-term development goals while fostering innovation, investment, and international cooperation in the renewable energy sector.
